name: ARP spoofing
description: Forged ARP messages can associate an attacker-controlled MAC with another host’s IPv4 address on the same LAN.
indicators: Traffic paths changing inside a VLAN
defenses: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection with a valid binding source
Use DHCP snooping and restrict access ports
Use authenticated encryption for sensitive traffic

name: On-path interception
description: An intermediary observes or modifies traffic between endpoints; compromised routing, access points, or trust anchors can enable it.
indicators: Differences between expected and received content
defenses: Validate peer identities and certificates
Use authenticated encryption
Protect network administration and trusted certificate stores

name: Distributed denial of service
description: Many sources or reflected responses exhaust a service’s network, connection, or application capacity.
indicators: Traffic exceeding baseline from many sources
High latency and timeouts under abnormal load
defenses: Use upstream filtering and an agreed response plan
Apply rate limits and resource budgets
Reduce exposed amplification services and monitor capacity

name: Port scanning
description: Probes identify reachable transport endpoints and sometimes infer services. Authorized scans are also a normal administration technique.
indicators: Connections to many unusual destination ports
defenses: Expose only required services
Record and investigate unusual scanning patterns
Use authenticated inventory to understand real exposure

name: VLAN hopping
description: A device attempts to reach another VLAN by exploiting trunk negotiation, tagging, or switch misconfiguration.
indicators: Unexpected tagged frames on access ports
defenses: Configure access and trunk modes explicitly
Restrict allowed VLANs on trunks
Apply routed access policies between security zones

name: DNS cache poisoning
description: Forged or compromised DNS data directs clients to unintended services by corrupting resolver answers.
indicators: Unexpected address changes without an authorized update
defenses: Use validating resolvers where DNSSEC is deployed
Restrict administrative and transfer access
Keep resolver software updated and monitor critical records

name: Rogue DHCP server
description: An unauthorized server supplies addresses, gateways, or resolvers to clients.
indicators: Clients receiving wrong gateway or DNS options
Address leases from an unapproved scope
defenses: Enable DHCP snooping with carefully selected trusted ports
Restrict physical and wireless access
Monitor offers and scope changes

name: Rogue Router Advertisement
description: Unauthorized IPv6 Router Advertisements can redirect hosts or disrupt their network configuration.
defenses: Deploy RA Guard appropriate to the switch implementation
Authorize router-facing ports explicitly
Monitor IPv6 even on primarily IPv4 networks

name: Credential stuffing
description: Previously exposed username and password pairs are tried against other services.
indicators: Repeated access to account recovery routes
defenses: Use passkeys or multifactor authentication
Rate-limit and monitor authentication
Encourage unique credentials and safe recovery flows

name: Server-side request forgery
description: An application is induced to make requests to unintended destinations using its own network access or identity.
indicators: Requests to internal or metadata addresses
Abnormal outbound requests from a lookup service
defenses: Use fixed upstream allowlists
Validate and constrain destination resolution and redirects
Limit response size, duration, and egress privileges

name: Route hijack
description: Incorrect or unauthorized routing advertisements divert or discard traffic for a prefix.
indicators: Sudden path changes for critical prefixes
defenses: Apply prefix and peer filtering
Use RPKI origin validation with operational policy
Monitor announcements and maintain an incident contact plan

name: Broadcast storm
description: Excessive broadcast traffic, often from a loop or malfunction, consumes link and endpoint resources.
indicators: Widespread LAN disruption without a WAN outage
defenses: Use loop-prevention mechanisms and edge-port protection
Set appropriate storm-control thresholds
Locate and remove the loop before restoring blocked links
